body:
With coroutine hooks enabled, `fclose()` on a `stream_socket_server()` listener returned before the descriptor was closed. Until the coroutine yielded, the listener still accepted connections and its address couldn't be bound again; native PHP releases it immediately. `Coroutine\Socket::close()`, which the hooked `socket_close()` also uses, kept the descriptor open for as long as the object existed.

A coroutine socket's descriptor was only closed by `network::Socket::free()`, which defers `close(fd)` to the end of the event loop pass, and `Coroutine\Socket::close()` never reached it. The unlink-and-close step of that deferred free is now `network::Socket::close_fd()`. It removes the socket's own bound UNIX path, closes the descriptor and invalidates it, so the later deferred free can neither unlink a replacement's path nor close a reused descriptor. `move_fd()` still only transfers ownership. The new `coroutine::Socket::close_fd()` shuts down SSL, removes the socket from the reactor and calls it. The release isn't done in `close()` itself: `swoole_coroutine_close()` erases the fd from the shared socket map only after `close()` returns, and another thread could reuse the number in between.

`~Socket()` releases the descriptor at once only after `close()` was called, which covers the hooked `fclose()` and `close()` paths. A socket destroyed while still open keeps the deferred release: closing it at once can reset a connection whose peer is still sending before the peer reads the final response, as `swoole_http_server_coro/error_413.phpt` shows with an in-process client.

`Coroutine\Socket::close()` now releases the descriptor once `close()` succeeds. When other coroutines are waiting on the socket, `close()` only cancels them and returns false, and nothing finished the close afterwards: the method returned true while `isClosed()` stayed false and the socket kept listening. It now finishes closing once the cancelled coroutines have left.

A bound UNIX path is now removed when the socket is closed rather than at the end of the event loop pass. Code that unlinks the path itself right after the hooked `socket_close()` or `fclose()` gets an ENOENT warning; Swoole 6.0 and earlier also removed the path synchronously when the socket was destroyed.

Three existing tests relied on the deferred close. `coroutine_socket.sendfile` now reads to EOF: it read once and closed the receiver while the sender could still be writing. `swoole_socket_coro/import_4.phpt` expected a socket imported from a stream to keep working after `fclose()` on that stream, although `import()` shares the descriptor. It now expects EBADF, as php-src's `socket_import_stream-4.phpt` does. `swoole_runtime/sockets/basic/bug76839.phpt` unlinks the receiver's path after `socket_close()`, so its cleanup now uses `@unlink()`.

`tests/swoole_runtime/stream_socket_server_close.phpt` and `tests/swoole_socket_coro/close_listener.phpt` check that a closed listener refuses connections and can be bound again immediately, including while another coroutine waits in `accept()`, and that the replacement still works after an event loop turn. `tests/swoole_socket_coro/close_unix_socket.phpt` checks UNIX stream and datagram sockets: the path can be bound again at once after `close()`, and after an event loop turn after destruction without `close()`, and each replacement still works after the old socket's deferred cleanup. They fail on unchanged `6.1` and pass with the fix, in both NTS and ZTS thread builds. The nearby `swoole_socket_coro`, `swoole_runtime`, `swoole_client_coro`, `swoole_server_coro`, `swoole_http_server_coro`, `swoole_http_client_coro` and `swoole_thread` PHPTs and the core socket tests show no new failures.


Hypervel regression: [test](https://github.com/hypervel/components/blob/6e6798b224c9b6f9456e8c6d42f1ef6cec84ac01/tests/Engine/HookedStreamTest.php#L38). This currently fails on affected Swoole versions.
